### 2026-10-14 – ### W dimensions

**0.3h**

### W dimensions

I sent out the motor holder to print. I do not count that time for this by the way. It was a 30-minute print, which wasn't too long.

When I got it back, it didn't fit very well so I hopped into CAD and changed it a bit. It took maybe 10 minutes to tweak it to how I think it's going to fit. It wasn't too hard and I got it to work for that. I have a little picture of it.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/RdWPsRxnKEEUTsz4xHbpaolVSJzlPoNU/f84972a7fee315e0deb0258909afd76730357e3c64aff6f7c4efd9a9f95a79ac.png)

I moved on to the actual base. I wanted to continue designing a bit more so I did.

I have the four-channel motor driver that I built a while ago so I'm planning on using that. I built it on a proto board so I just got the dimensions from that and started designing a little enclosure for it. The enclosure doesn't look too bad; it's just a little box.

While I was designing it, I encountered a tiny flaw: my actual base wasn't centered and was off by about 1 cm. I thought it looked weird but I really didn't think much of it so I had to go in and fix that. Dimensions and shape are very scary so it took me a bit. It looks good now. I filleted the edges and added screw holes so it's all good so far. Image here

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/RdWPsRxnKEEUTsz4xHbpaolVSJzlPoNU/154df3ab21378d709e35edba93340dcfe91c10c3125e75048a8dce9a09a6575b.png)

### 2026-10-15 – ### OmniWheel

**0.75h**

### OmniWheel

It was time for the scariest part of this entire project. I was away from my printer today so I couldn't print or work on anything else. I decided to start the OmniWheel. It's actually called the mechnum wheel but I'm only familiar with the OmniWheel so I just call it that.

OmniWheels can move in any direction. They can go forward and backward like normal wheels but they also go side to side, which is the really cool part about them. I had no idea at all how to start this in CAD so I watched a YouTube video (which I did not count as time) about how to make this. I implemented some of the strategies they used.

I learned quite a bit about actual CAD and related tools because this forced me to use different pieces I had never used before. Here are the pictures of them: one from the top and two of them connected. I still have to make the little rollers but it shouldn't be too bad. I'll see you guys tomorrow.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/RdWPsRxnKEEUTsz4xHbpaolVSJzlPoNU/11f1ce15c055ae7bce8d8dc38f492e41bead4d98ce15756306f6392dcd8f5326.png)

### 2026-10-16 – ### Roller

**0.6h**

### Roller

I took a bit of time. I had robotics earlier today, so I have an Omni wheel I could use as a basis for modeling the roller. Since I don't have any TPU, I adjusted it to have just a lot of grooves, which was probably the hardest part of making this. I wanted quite a few, so I was able to get that.

I then wanted it to connect well to the other halves, so I made a little thing. I had to change the dimensions of the part I made last time so I did. It took me maybe 5 minutes and wasn't hard at all.

Now I'm going to go print the parts and see if they actually fit together. Here are some images for you.

### 2026-10-17 – So I printed a version out and I put a roller into the mechnum wheel and it worked pretty well. The tolerances were a little off so I had to adjust that a bit. It was really flimsy and weak so I had t

**1h**

So I printed a version out and I put a roller into the mechnum wheel and it worked pretty well. The tolerances were a little off so I had to adjust that a bit. It was really flimsy and weak so I had to make it a bit thicker so I did that. I also now made a way to connect two of them together using screws and heat-set inserts. This was really hard because I kept messing up the measurements. In turn I had to do a bit of :Shiver: math. It was really scary but it took me 5 minutes for the math and like 30 to add it all t , yes i know it was slow but I am not the best at cad. Here is some images

### 2026-10-18 – ### Assembly and tolerances

**1h**

### Assembly and tolerances

I printed it. I sent it overnight. It was, I think, only an hour so it printed pretty quickly. I got the part and I tried inserting into the motor, but it wouldn't fit at all so I messed up the tolerances for that. I also only had one screw hole, which I thought would be enough, but I am going to switch to four holes so I can have good tolerance and make sure it doesn't wobble to the side a bunch.

Other than that I made a little assembly to make sure everything fits like I wanted because that was a big problem with the last one. It looks pretty good. I haven't done much assembly so I had to learn stuff. That wasn't too bad and here's a little image of what I made.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/RdWPsRxnKEEUTsz4xHbpaolVSJzlPoNU/f1c36bce70a067e3d71c2eca05d0365860ee31497ea855e7587853e6cc95603c.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/RdWPsRxnKEEUTsz4xHbpaolVSJzlPoNU/5cd581fed74ddfd12af755a07b3101f5af260e16690ece9d0a833ea3dbc9c335.png)

### 2026-10-18 – ### Done

**1h**

### Done

I spent about 60 minutes working on this.

I started with the actual chassis and added two small compartments on the side for batteries, sensors, and similar items. Apart from adding more storage, this also makes the frame much more durable, which is really good.

I also finished the motor holder. After many prototypes it now fits the motor well. It has screw holes so I can just screw the motor in, which is nice.

The mechnum wheel finished printing so I went and grabbed it, then assembled everything. Assembly took maybe 10 to 15 minutes. It looks okay but there is a lot of friction, which is the main problem. Because of that friction I didn't feel comfortable using it in the actual build because the grip isn't strong. There is nothing special about it, it is not very tight, and it can fall off very easily. I will probably just buy some wheels for the actual build.

Now I'm going to create a GitHub repo for everything. Here are some images of the wheel and chassis.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/RdWPsRxnKEEUTsz4xHbpaolVSJzlPoNU/7a027561b33ab733330398e755ec4e44070d464df7d59fcae121645e8a5fa4b3.png)
